facts.fact: The World Bank's appraisal document of 18 September 2025 proposes an IDA credit of EUR 128.6 million (US$150.0 million equivalent) for RAPID-CI phase 1, which is to expand connectivity in key public facilities including town halls; no date is given for the connection itself, so the document's date is used.
facts.system: Results Acceleration Program for Inclusive Digitalization in Côte d'Ivoire (RAPID-CI) phase 1

facts.fact: The appraisal document of 18 September 2025 says that, under the second pillar of the national digital transformation strategy (a connected government), the project aims to connect more than 1,300 schools, hospitals, courts and municipalities to high-speed internet, especially in rural and disadvantaged areas, phase 1 covering selected regions and phase 2 the country; it gives no separate count of municipalities.
facts.system: Results Acceleration Program for Inclusive Digitalization in Côte d'Ivoire (RAPID-CI) phase 1

facts.fact: The appraisal document of 18 September 2025 presents the programme as the government's, prepared by the digital ministry (MTND) with the ministries of health, education, justice, interior, public administration and social protection, under a Project Steering Committee already established.
facts.system: Results Acceleration Program for Inclusive Digitalization in Côte d'Ivoire (RAPID-CI) phase 1

facts.fact: The appraisal document of 18 September 2025 states that an ongoing EU-funded project implemented by CIVIPOL covers the connectivity of town halls, with which the World Bank programme will coordinate; it gives no count of town halls and no amount.
facts.system: EU-funded project implemented by CIVIPOL (connectivity of town halls)

facts.fact: The appraisal document of 18 September 2025 describes the ongoing project for the connectivity of town halls as funded by the European Union and implemented by CIVIPOL.
facts.system: EU-funded project implemented by CIVIPOL (connectivity of town halls)
